minutes.headline: Superintendent presented a first draft FY20 school budget with cut positions listed; four policies approved
minutes.summary: The new superintendent and business manager presented the preliminary FY20 school budget, naming requested positions and which were struck for now. Committee members questioned the cut positions, and parents and residents spoke on kindergarten class size and tax burden. Four policies were approved on third reading, and the committee went into executive session.

what_happened.line: The superintendent and business manager presented a first draft FY20 school budget, naming requested positions and which were struck for now.
Health insurance was budgeted at an eight percent increase, with an added cost for each new benefited employee.
Four policies (petty cash, agenda format, public participation, petitions) were approved on third reading; the vote count was not audible.
Residents and parents spoke on kindergarten class size, paraprofessional placement, and whether budget growth can be sustained under Prop 2 1/2.
The committee set kindergarten registration for early February and added the open space plan to the January 2nd agenda.

why_it_matters: The draft budget sets the starting point for the school share of next year's tax bill, and the positions struck or kept decide class sizes and support staff, including in kindergarten.
Budget growth above the Prop 2 1/2 limit on revenue growth can lead to cuts or to an override vote that residents would be asked to take.
watch_next: Release of the preliminary Chapter 70 state aid figure ahead of the February meeting.
The January 2nd School Committee agenda, which is to include the open space plan.
